We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have guidance: reactions enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). They gave hints: Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution (halogenation). So retrosynthesis steps likely reverse: start from target, break into precursors via reverse of these reactions.

We need to produce JSON route with type mol root target, children reaction nodes (3). Each reaction node includes template_id (need to find appropriate template IDs). We can search for templates matching each transformation.

First step: maybe disconnection of amide bond (NC(=O)...) via reverse of amide formation (i.e., break amide to give amine and acyl chloride?). But hints mention substitution (replace OH with halogen) maybe for converting phenol to aryl halide for Friedel-Crafts? Let's examine target: aromatic ring with methoxy (CO) at position 1, and an anilide (NC(=O)...) attached to same ring. The amide attaches to heterocycle (c2nnn(... )c2N). So maybe retrosynthesis: break amide to give aniline (NH2) and acyl chloride (or acid). Then Friedel-Crafts acylation to attach acyl onto anisole? Actually Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl onto aromatic ring; here we have anisole ring (methoxy phenyl) with amide substituent. Could be formed by Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole with acyl chloride derived from heterocycle (c2nnn...). Then Sn2 to attach side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 onto the heterocycle via alkyl halide substitution.

Let's search for template for amide bond formation reverse (i.e., amide cleavage). Search functional_groups_broken ["amide"] gave template 647549 which seems to break amide into amine and carboxylic acid? The retro_smarts_template: [O;D1;H0:2]=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[NH;D2;+0:8]-[c:9])-[c:3]1...>> O-[C;...]. That seems to break amide into carboxylic acid and amine. Good.

We need template_id = 647549.

Second step: Friedel-Crafts acylation reverse (i.e., break aryl-CO bond). Search for functional_groups_broken ["acyl chloride"]? Actually forward Friedel-Crafts acylation forms carbonyl attached to aromatic, breaking halide (Cl). So reverse would break carbonyl-aryl bond to give aryl and acyl chloride. Search for functional_groups_broken ["aryl halide"] maybe. Let's search.
